description: Every POS station (till, register, checkout lane, cash desk) the merchant has — the same list as Run → Stations. Answers 'how many tills do I have', 'which register is busy right now', 'which store is this till at', 'which of them are browser tills'. Each station belongs to exactly ONE outlet and the outlet name is resolved here, so you do not need get_outlets to answer where a till stands — call get_outlets only to turn a store NAME the merchant said into the outletId filter of this tool. WHAT status MEANS, EXACTLY: the server does not compute it. The POS app on the till writes it — IN_USE when a cashier opens a register shift on that station, AVAILABLE when the shift is closed. It is best-effort: the update is lost while the device is offline and only flushed when it reconnects, and older app versions never sent it at all, so a station can sit at AVAILABLE with a shift open on it or at IN_USE hours after one was closed. Read it as "what this till last told us", never as proof. NEVER answer a shift or money question from it: for shifts that are actually open, who opened them and what they took, use get_sessions (a session with no closeTime is open) and get_session_report. If those disagree with this flag, they are right and the flag is stale. The whole list comes back in one call — it is short and plan-capped, there is no paging; search matches the station NAME only. Deleted stations are not returned.

kind.description: native = a physical device running the POS app; virtual = a browser till

outletId.description: Only stations at this outlet — id from get_outlets, not a store name

status.description: IN_USE = the till last reported an open register shift; AVAILABLE = it did not

name: hub_get_stations
title: List tills
